messages:
lia (docs): quick heads-up — I'm opening a docs PR to replace the older callback-based streaming examples with an async-iterator/cursor pattern across py/ts/go. aim: consistent retry semantics + clearer pagination examples. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4321
kevin (eng-runtime): nice. can you call out the behaviour for partial prefixes/KV cache hits? that's where folks usually get surprised.
sophie (eng-ml): also add a short note on quality regressions when switching quantized models — we saw truncated tokens in one flow.
lia (docs): good call, @kevin @sophie — i'll add an explicit note and a small table. thinking of including minimal examples:
- python async iterator with exponential backoff retry (client-side)
- typescript streaming using for-await-of with cursor resume
- go channel-based stream + example of idempotent resume token

kevin (eng-runtime): sample snippet for TS please show `max_retries` and `backoff_jitter` usage. small code block:
```ts
for await (const chunk of client.stream({ model: 'redwood-mini', input: prompt })) {
  // handle chunk.text
}
```
lia (docs): adding that. also cc @anna (eng-platform) for snippet test infra — CI is failing on one of the python snippets in the snippet-harness job.
ci-bot: snippet-harness: failed tests in job `docs-snippets` — failing file: examples/py/stream_cursor_retry.py line 47 (timeout). See logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234
anna (eng-platform): looking. usually the harness needs a small sleep added for local sockets — will debug. if it's a real flake we can add `# noqa:SNIPPET_TIMEOUT` for now.
sophie (eng-ml): For the Go sample, prefer showing how to use context.WithTimeout and reattach using a resume token; simple example below. keeps it idiomatic.
lia (docs): drafting three tiny files to keep copy-paste friendly. also adding a migration note for users moving from callback-style `on_chunk` -> `async for` patterns. sample migration blurb: "Replace event callbacks with the streaming iterator to simplify backpressure and make retries composable."
kevin (eng-runtime): we should also document server-side behaviour: when we return a resume token and what guarantees it gives (best-effort, not durable across model variant). i'll write a short paragraph and drop in the PR.
lia (docs): thanks — would you add that under `Streaming semantics`? label it "resume token guarantees".
kevin (eng-runtime): will do.
lia (docs): reviewers: @kevin @sophie @anna — ping when you can. small ask: prefer inline comment on lines 12-30 where the example live.
kevin (eng-runtime): skimmed — left two inline comments about KV cache and a formatting nit. :eyes:
anna (eng-platform): fixed the harness timeout and re-ran. CI looks green now except one lint: snippet filenames must be kebab-case.
lia (docs): changed filenames and pushed. one remaining question: do we keep the old callback examples anywhere? i'd prefer a short archived section "legacy callbacks" with a clear deprecation note.
sophie (eng-ml): archive them under a legacy/ folder, yes. add a line: "Use iterators for new code; callbacks deprecated for new integrations."
lia (docs): ok added. merging after final thumbs. cc docs-bot to create a follow-up issue to add QA test for resume token regression.
docs-bot: created issue #678: "add regression test for streaming resume token semantics" assigned to eng-ml.
kevin (eng-runtime): one more: add a tiny note about cost implications of long-lived streaming connections (token accounting) — folks miss that.
lia (docs): good point, added a line under "costs & best practices".
anna (eng-platform): quick FYI: when landing, tag release-notes with `docs: streaming examples` so SDK teams can sync.
lia (docs): will do. merging in ~30m if no objections. thanks all! :tada:
